questions.title: What exactly is the Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) objective and how does it differ from standard PPO?
questions.question_body: I read the section introducing GRPO and see Equation (4) defining \( \mathcal{J}_{GRPO}(\theta) \). However, I am unclear on three points: (1) how the advantage \( \hat{A}_{i,t} \) is computed using group-relative rewards, (2) why the KL regularization term is added directly to the loss instead of being part of the reward as in PPO, and (3) what practical benefits (e.g., memory savings, stability) arise from removing the critic/value network. Could someone walk through a concrete example of a single question with a group of sampled outputs?

questions.title: How is the DeepSeekMath corpus de‑duplicated and filtered to avoid benchmark contamination?
questions.question_body: The paper mentions URL‑based deduplication, near‑deduplication, and a 10‑gram exact‑match filter for GSM8K/MATH/CMATH etc. I am confused about the exact pipeline: after deduplication, are pages scored by the fastText classifier and then ranked? At what point is the 10‑gram filter applied, and does it operate on raw HTML or extracted text? Also, how does the "10% domain" rule for identifying math‑related domains work in practice?

questions.title: Why does pre‑training on arXiv papers not improve mathematical reasoning in DeepSeekMath?
questions.question_body: The authors report that training on MathPile or ArXiv‑RedPajama gave no gains (or even hurt) performance on GSM8K, MATH, MMLU‑STEM, and miniF2F. Is this because the arXiv data lacks the step‑by‑step reasoning style found in benchmark problems, or could it be due to token distribution differences? How was the arXiv‑only corpus prepared (e.g., LaTeX removal) and could different preprocessing or larger model scales change this conclusion?

questions.title: What is the role of code pre‑training before math pre‑training, and why does it help?
questions.question_body: The paper conducts two‑stage experiments where a 1.3B model first sees 400B code tokens then 150B math tokens, and also a mixed one‑stage variant. The results show improvements in program‑aided reasoning but mixed training sometimes harms pure reasoning. I am trying to understand: (a) what aspects of code data (e.g., syntax, execution semantics) transfer to symbolic math reasoning, (b) why catastrophic forgetting occurs when code is only in the first stage for a small model, and (c) whether larger models would benefit more from mixed code+math training.

questions.title: How are outcome supervision and process supervision implemented in GRPO?
questions.question_body: The paper describes outcome supervision as assigning the same normalized reward to all tokens of an output, while process supervision provides step‑wise rewards. I am unsure how "steps" are detected in generated text (e.g., via special tokens or line breaks), how the per‑step rewards are normalized across a group, and how the advantage \( \hat{A}_{i,t} = \sum_{index(j)\ge t}\widetilde{r}_i^{index(j)} \) propagates back to earlier tokens. Could someone clarify with an example of a CoT answer containing three reasoning steps?

questions.title: Why does reinforcement learning mainly improve Maj@K rather than Pass@K according to Figure 8?
questions.question_body: The authors state that RL makes the output distribution more robust, boosting correct responses from TopK but not changing fundamental capability. How is Maj@K computed in this context (majority vote over multiple samples per question?), and why would GRPO’s group‑relative baseline lead to higher probability mass on already good answers rather than generating better new solutions? Is this an artifact of using only outcome supervision with a reward model trained on correctness?

questions.title: What does "iterative RL with GRPO" entail and how does replaying 10% of historic data affect training?
questions.question_body: Algorithm 1 mentions updating the reward model after each iteration using a replay buffer that contains 10% historical samples. I am confused about: (i) how new training pairs for the reward model are generated from the current policy, (ii) why only 10% of old data is kept instead of full history, and (iii) what impact this has on stability or preventing reward drift across iterations.

questions.title: How does self‑consistency over 64 samples raise DeepSeekMath’s MATH score from 51.7% to 60.9%?
questions.question_body: The abstract says self‑consistency over 64 samples yields 60.9% on MATH. Is this simply taking a majority vote over 64 independently sampled CoT answers per question? If so, why does increasing sample count help so dramatically for this model compared to others? Does GRPO’s training encourage higher variance among samples that can be aggregated effectively?

questions.title: Can the unified paradigm (Equation 9) be used to derive DPO as a special case of PPO/GRPO?
questions.question_body: The authors claim that supervised fine‑tuning, RFT, DPO, PPO, and GRPO can all be expressed with gradient coefficient \(GC_{\mathcal{A}}\). I would like to see an explicit derivation showing how DPO’s pairwise loss fits into this framework—what choices of data source, reward function \(\pi_{rf}\), and algorithm produce the DPO gradient coefficient? This would help me understand the connections between these methods.
